title: Network-Herding Momentum-Reversal Transition Signal on H198 Stock Universe
source: arXiv:2607.27063 (Jul 2026) — "Herding, Momentum, and Reversal in China's A-Share Market: An Agent-Based Network Model with Information Diffusion" (Anonymous)
description: The paper provides a theoretical mechanism for why momentum eventually flips to reversal: local herding (investors copying neighbors) generates initial momentum, but as information diffuses fully through the network, the herding effect saturates and reversal emerges. This suggests a momentum-age signal: stocks that have experienced momentum for longer periods are closer to the herding saturation point and closer to reversal. H477 tests whether conditioning on the 'age' of a momentum streak (how many consecutive months a stock has ranked in the top momentum quintile) improves selection: young-momentum stocks (1-3 months in top quintile) should continue; old-momentum stocks (6+ months) should be avoided or shorted.
content_summary: The paper develops an agent-based model where investors on a lattice/network form heterogeneous Gaussian beliefs about next-period price, choose buy/sell/inactive, and revise action probabilities based on neighboring investors. Local herding creates positive autocorrelation (momentum) in the short run. As information propagates through the network with delay, the entire network eventually aligns — at which point the herding effect reverses direction (late adopters become contrarians). Key empirical calibration on China A-shares: momentum phase lasts 3-9 months, reversal phase starts at 9-18 months — broadly consistent with Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) US momentum. For H477 US large-cap adaptation (H198 30-stock universe): the 6-1m skip-month signal already avoids the 1-month reversal, but does not account for momentum age. Proposed signal: add a 'momentum streak counter' — number of consecutive months each stock has ranked in top-6 by 6-1m momentum. Gate: old-momentum stocks (top-6 for 6+ consecutive months) receive a penalty to their momentum score (or are excluded), focusing selection on younger momentum candidates. Alternative: test whether stocks NEW to the top-6 (entering from bottom half) generate stronger forward returns than stocks that have been in top-6 for 3+ months (mature momentum).
variants: Var A: Exclude stocks with 6+ consecutive months in top-6 momentum rank; select from remaining universe
Var B: Penalize momentum score by streak length: adj_score = raw_score * (1 - 0.05 * min(streak, 6))
Var C: Overweight NEW entrants to top-6 (first month in top-6): double weight vs incumbents
Var D: Momentum reversal gate — if stock in top-6 for 9+ months, route to short instead
Var E: H198 baseline 6-1m top-6 (sanity check)
gate: OOS Sharpe > 1.174 (H198 baseline) AND MaxDD improvement
data_requirements: yfinance price data for H198 30-stock universe (already used). Streak counter: state variable tracking how many consecutive months each stock has been in top-6 by 6-1m momentum rank. State maintained across monthly rebalance.
implementation_notes: Streak counter implementation: at each monthly rebalance, check if stock was in top-6 last month. If yes, streak[stock] += 1. If no, streak[stock] = 0. When computing adjusted momentum score for Var B: adj_score_i = raw_momentum_i * exp(-0.1 * streak_i) for continuous decay. For Var A: filter universe to exclude any stock with streak >= 6 before running top-6 selection. Theoretical prediction: US large-cap universe has faster information diffusion than China A-shares (more institutional investors, smaller network diameter), so saturation may occur at shorter streak lengths (3-4 months vs 6-9 months in China). Test streak thresholds 3, 4, 5, 6 in IS period. CAUTION: H198 30-stock NASDAQ universe is small — removing mature-momentum stocks may leave fewer candidates, concentrating the portfolio. Monitor portfolio concentration. If top-6 becomes top-3 after exclusions, consider relaxing to top-8 before applying streak filter.
